prompt.zh-TW: 佩珊在分析晨光印刷還不還得出錢時，把「融資維持率」和公司自己的償債指標排在一起比較。哪一個提醒最正確？
prompt.en: While analysing whether Morning Light Printing can pay its debts, Pei-shan lists the margin maintenance ratio alongside the company’s own solvency measures. Which reminder is correct?

text.zh-TW: 它是投資人信用交易帳戶的指標，和公司的償債能力無關
text.en: It belongs to an investor’s margin account and says nothing about the company’s solvency

feedback.zh-TW: 答對了。融資維持率算的是投資人的擔保品夠不夠抵借款，不是公司的資產與負債；公司還不還得出錢，要看公司自己的流動比率與利息保障倍數。
feedback.en: That is right. The margin maintenance ratio measures whether an investor’s collateral covers the loan, not the company’s assets and liabilities; whether the company can pay its debts is read from its own current ratio and times interest earned.

text.zh-TW: 它和流動比率一樣，都在衡量公司短期還得出錢的能力
text.en: Like the current ratio, it measures the company’s ability to pay in the short term

feedback.zh-TW: 你抓到了「比率越低越危險」的共通感覺。但危險的對象不同：維持率低是投資人要被追繳，不是公司還不出錢。
feedback.en: You picked up the shared sense that lower is riskier. But the party at risk differs: a low maintenance ratio means the investor faces a margin call, not that the company cannot pay.

text.zh-TW: 它衡量的是公司自己借了多少錢來放大獲利
text.en: It measures how much the company itself has borrowed to magnify its profit

feedback.zh-TW: 融資的確是一種槓桿，但那是投資人的槓桿；公司的財務槓桿看它自己借了多少錢，和投資人用不用融資無關。
feedback.en: Margin is indeed leverage, but it is the investor’s leverage; a company’s financial leverage depends on how much it borrowed itself, regardless of whether investors use margin.

explanation.zh-TW: {{option:o_f4g5}}把兩套帳分開了。{{option:o_h6j7}}與{{option:o_k8m9}}都把投資人的指標套到公司身上。
explanation.en: {{option:o_f4g5}} keeps the two sets of accounts apart. {{option:o_h6j7}} and {{option:o_k8m9}} both apply an investor’s measure to the company.
